title: Ogoma's lemma
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $M$ a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and $S\subset A$ a multiplicative subset, with $S^{-1}M$ the localization of $M$ at $S$ [def-weil-pbc-module-localization]. Let $\pi\in A$ and suppose $\operatorname{Ker}(\pi:S^{-1}M\to S^{-1}M)=\operatorname{Ker}(\pi^2:S^{-1}M\to S^{-1}M)$. Then there is $s\in S$ such that for every integer $n>0$, $\operatorname{Ker}(s^n\pi:M\to M)=\operatorname{Ker}((s^n\pi)^2:M\to M)$.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FC (lemma-ogoma, line 2287), Section 07FB

proof.text: Let f : M → S⁻¹M be the localization map and g : M → M multiplication by π. Set K′ = ker(f ∘ g ∘ g) and N = g(K′), both submodules of M. The image N realizes the quotient K′/ker(g) in the original argument, without needing a quotient or an isomorphism in Lean.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FC (lemma-ogoma, line 2287), Section 07FB

proof.text: For x ∈ N choose m ∈ K′ with g(m)=x. Then π² f(m)=0. The assumed equality of kernels gives π f(m)=0, hence f(x)=0. The localization kernel criterion gives t ∈ S with tx=0. Equality in the submodule follows by injectivity of its inclusion. Thus S⁻¹N=0 by LocalizedModule.subsingleton_iff.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FC (lemma-ogoma, line 2287), Section 07FB

proof.text: N is a submodule of the finite module M over the Noetherian ring A, so N is finite. Mathlib infers IsNoetherian A N and Module.Finite A N from the ambient instances.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FC (lemma-ogoma, line 2287), Section 07FB

proof.text: Apply Module.exists_annihilator_of_subsingleton_localizedModule to N to obtain s ∈ S annihilating N. Consequently sπm=0 for every m ∈ K′.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FC (lemma-ogoma, line 2287), Section 07FB

proof.text: Fix n>0. If sⁿπm=0, multiplying once more gives (sⁿπ)²m=0. Conversely, if (sⁿπ)²m=0, the identity (sⁿπ)²=s^(n+n)π² and linearity show s^(n+n) f(π²m)=0. Since s^(n+n) belongs to S, multiplication by it on the localization is injective, giving f(π²m)=0. Thus m ∈ K′ and sπm=0. Write n=k+1; then sⁿπm=s^k(sπm)=0. Extensionality gives the asserted set equality.

source.place: Smoothing Ring Maps, Lemma Tag 07FC (lemma-ogoma, line 2287), Section 07FB
